description: Team DHARTIX (Dharti + X) is a 2-member team from KGCE, Karjat building a decision-support tool that helps farmers explore climate-resilient crop rotations by combining NASA Earth observations like POWER temperature, GPM rainfall and SMAP soil moisture with local soil health, crop characteristics and farmer priorities like water, time and cost, where farmers can select their field, see how monsoon onset has shifted
summary:
DhartiX is a free web app that gives small farmers simple crop advice for their own village. A farmer shares their location, field size, soil and irrigation, and gets a plan in English, Hindi or Marathi. It tells them whether it will rain in the next 16 days, which crop to grow and when to sow, how much water they need, and what profit to expect.

It uses open NASA data (NASA POWER climate history and NASA GIBS satellite layers), combined with a live weather forecast and local soil data. The app turns this into clear advice: sow now, wait, irrigate or skip. If live data fails to load, it says so instead of showing made-up numbers.

This matters because a wrong sowing date or crop choice can cost a small farmer a whole season's income, and most farmers have no easy way to use satellite data. DhartiX is free, needs no sign-up, and works on any phone, so it brings that data to farmers who are usually left out. It is a prototype, so advice should be confirmed with local soil tests and agriculture officers.
details:
What it does and how it works: DhartiX is a free web app that gives small farmers crop advice for their own village. The farmer shares their location, field size, soil and irrigation. The app then shows whether it will rain in the next 16 days, which crop to grow, when to sow, how much water is needed and what profit to expect. It gets NASA POWER climate data, a live Open-Meteo forecast and SoilGrids soil data, scores each crop for each month, and gives a clear message: sow now, wait, irrigate or skip.

Benefits:It helps farmers avoid wasted seed, water and money. It is free, needs no sign-up and works on any phone. It speaks English, Hindi and Marathi and can read advice aloud. If live data fails, it says so instead of showing fake numbers.

Intended impact:To make NASA and weather data useful to small farmers, so they make better sowing and crop decisions, use water carefully and protect their soil. Real-world impact is not measured yet, since this is a prototype.


Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single file, the Leaflet map library, NASA POWER and NASA GIBS, Open-Meteo, SoilGrids and OpenStreetMap. It needs no special hardware, only a phone or computer with a browser and internet. Please add the editor and tools your team used.

Creativity:It turns complex satellite data into one simple sentence, links weather to profit, and combines several data sources on one page. It works in local languages, with voice and WhatsApp sharing, and needs no server.

Factors considered:Farmers' low literacy and basic phones, free access, honest data limits (NASA data is coarse, about 50 km), local seasons and crops, privacy (nothing is stored), and safe advice that should be confirmed with local soil tests and agriculture officers.
dataRefs: NASA POWER, daily and monthly point data (rain, temperature, soil wetness)
NASA GIBS, map layers for MODIS true colour, MODIS NDVI, IMERG rainfall and MODIS land temperature
projectRefs: ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0 (clay, sand, silt, organic carbon, pH)
Esri World Imagery (satellite base map tiles)
BigDataCloud Reverse Geocoding (place name from GPS)
